my_time.title: My time

cannot_hand_in.month_running: The month is not over yet. It can be handed in once it has ended.
cannot_hand_in.timer_running: Stop the timer that is still running, then hand the month in.

toasts.not_recomputed: Could not bring it up to date

my_time.no_record_detail: Your hours are not being tracked in this workspace. If they should be, ask whoever looks after the team to set you up.

team_time.title: Team time
team_time.not_permitted: This is not yours to see
team_time.counted_anywhere: Everyone's hours are counted wherever they logged them. Closing a month freezes its figures; nothing recorded afterwards changes them.
team_time.as_things_stand: Figures are as things stand on {date}; the month is not over.
team_time.not_permitted_detail: Everyone's hours are only readable by whoever looks after the team. Your own month is on {page}.
team_time.confirm_close_body: The figures are frozen as they stand, and the hours, absences and attendance behind them stop accepting changes. Reopening it later is possible but leaves a trail.

summary.as_of: As things stand on {date}. The month is not over.
summary.not_started: This month has not started yet.
summary.needs_review: Some days need looking at — hours that were counted before are no longer there.
summary.timer_running: A timer is still running, so this month cannot be handed in yet.
summary.nothing_yet: Nothing has been worked out for this month yet.

day_table.not_yet: This day has not happened yet.
day_table.needs_review: Hours counted here earlier are no longer there
day_table.nothing_yet: Nothing has been worked out for this month yet.
day_table.rest_of_month: {count, plural, one {Show the rest of the month (# day)} other {Show the rest of the month (# days)}}
day_table.hide_rest_of_month: Hide the rest of the month

overview_table.nobody_yet: Nobody has an employment record yet.
overview_table.month_running: The month is not over yet

reopen.title: Reopen {month}?
reopen.body: {person}'s month has been closed and its figures frozen. Reopening keeps the closed version and records this one alongside it — nothing that was agreed is overwritten.
reopen.label: Why is it being reopened?
reopen.placeholder: Three days in the second week were logged against the wrong month.

people.title: People
people.subtitle: Who the company employs, and the terms each of them works under.
people.nobody_yet: Nobody has an employment record yet. Add someone to start counting their hours.
people.footnote: Somebody who leaves is marked as having left rather than removed, so the months they worked stay readable.
people.not_permitted_detail: Only whoever looks after the team can change who is employed and on what terms.
people.add_hint: Pick the account whose hours this record will count.
people.everybody_added: Everybody already has an employment record.
people.modal_hint: Terms and a working week decide what this person's month comes to, so they are set together.
people.is_manager: Looks after the team — can see and change everyone's hours, absences and leave, in every workspace
people.records_target: Record hours owed and a running balance
people.records_target_hint: Off for self-invoicing arrangements, where the company records what was worked and nothing is owed by the day.
people.schedule_hint: Hours owed on each day. Type 7:42 or 7.7, and leave a day blank when it is not worked.

errors.bad_duration: One of the days is not a length of time. Type 7:42 or 7.7, or leave it blank.
errors.hire_date_required: Say when this person started, so their first month knows where to begin.
errors.week_required: Say how long each working day is, so their month has something to be measured against.
errors.bad_crm_staff_id: A CRM staff id is a whole number. Leave it empty to match on the email address instead.

people.crm_staff_id_placeholder: Leave empty to match by email

crm_link.set: Set here, so the hours go to this account whatever the addresses say.
crm_link.email: Matched by email address. It works until one of the two systems has a different one.
crm_link.none: Nothing joins this person to the CRM, so their hours never become a CRM timer.

people.confirm_remove_body: {person} stops appearing in new months. Everything already recorded stays as it is.
people.confirm_remove_permanent: You can employ them again later if they come back.
people.pick_somebody_first: Pick somebody from the list first
people.nobody_matches_detail: Only people who already have an account here can be given an employment record. Accounts are created in Workspace settings, under Members.
people.everybody_added_detail: Everyone with an account here already has an employment record.

entries.hint: Time that no work item accounts for — meetings, admin, training, travel.
entries.none_yet: Nothing recorded on this day yet.
entries.note_placeholder: What this time was spent on
entries.month_closed: This month has been closed, so its hours can no longer be changed. Ask whoever looks after the team if something needs correcting.

errors.bad_duration: Say how long it was. Type 1:30 or 1.5.

entries.confirm_remove_body: {duration} comes off this day and off the month's total.

attendance.title: When you were at work
attendance.hint: Start, end and breaks for this day, kept separately from what the hours went on.
attendance.closed_with: {from} to {to}, {duration}. This month has been closed, so it can no longer be changed.
attendance.closed_without: Nothing was recorded for this day, and the month has been closed.

errors.bad_break: Give the break in whole minutes.

attendance.confirm_remove_body: The start, end and break for this day are removed. This is the record of working time the law asks to be kept.
attendance.past_midnight_length: This runs past midnight and comes to {duration}. Check the end time if that is not right.

imports.title: Bring hours in
imports.subtitle: Months recorded somewhere else, read from a spreadsheet and checked before anything is written.
imports.not_permitted_detail: Only whoever looks after the team can bring hours in.

columns.time_entries: Columns: email, date, and either hours or minutes — those exact headings. A note column is kept if there is one. 7:42, 7.7 and 462 all read as the same length of time.
columns.absences: Columns: email, start_date, end_date and type — those exact headings. Leave end_date out for a single day.
columns.opening_balances: Columns: email, effective_on for the day it applies from, and either hours or minutes for the balance itself — those exact headings.

imports.preview_hint: Nothing has been written yet. Check the rows below, then apply.
imports.none_yet: Nothing has been brought in yet.
imports.row_summary: {total, plural, one {{valid} of # row} other {{valid} of # rows}}
imports.undo_body: Every hour this file wrote is removed, and nothing else is touched. Hours in a month that has since been closed stay where they are.

toasts.written: {count, plural, one {# row written} other {# rows written}}
toasts.removed: {count, plural, one {# row removed} other {# rows removed}}

reasons.bad_date: The date could not be read.
reasons.bad_duration: The amount of time could not be read.
reasons.more_than_a_day: More than a day in a single day.
reasons.month_settled: That month has been closed already.
reasons.bad_balance: The balance could not be read.
reasons.kind_missing: Say whether this is time or leave.
reasons.basis_missing: Say what this figure is based on.
reasons.bad_start_date: The start date could not be read.

opening.title: {person}'s starting balance
opening.hint: Where this person stood on the day counting started here. There is no history to work these out from, which is why they are agreed rather than derived — so each one keeps what it was based on, and the person it belongs to says whether they accept it.
opening.none_yet: No starting balance has been recorded yet, so counting begins from zero.
opening.replaced: {count, plural, one {# replaced by a correction} other {# replaced by a correction}}
opening.basis_placeholder: Carried over from the leave spreadsheet, checked against the March payslip

errors.bad_duration: Say how much. Type -12:30 or -12.5, or leave off the minus for a surplus.
errors.basis_required: Say what this figure is based on. A number nobody can account for is one nobody can defend when the person it belongs to disagrees.
errors.date_required: Say which day this balance applies from.

opening.confirm_agree_body: You are agreeing that {amount} is right. This cannot be taken back. If the figure is wrong, do not agree to it — say so to whoever looks after the team.

absences.title: Absences
absences.subtitle: Time away from work, and what it does to the month.
absences.not_permitted_detail: Only a manager sees the whole team. Your own absences are on your time page.

granularity.hours: A set number of hours a day

modal.title: Record an absence
modal.subtitle: Where the reason counts as worked, the day is credited so the month still comes out level. The target itself does not change.
modal.backwards: The last day cannot come before the first.
modal.hours_unreadable: That is not a length of time. Try 1:30, 1,5 or 90.

types.title: Reasons for being away
types.subtitle: Two answers decide the arithmetic: whether the day still counts as worked, and whether it comes off the leave account.
types.counts_as_worked: The day still counts as worked
types.draws_on_leave: The day comes off the leave account
types.confirm_remove_body: “{kind}” will no longer be offered when somebody records an absence. Switch it off instead if you only want it out of the list.

absences.confirm_remove_body: {person} goes back to a full target for those days, and {duration} returns to their leave.
absences.refuse_body: They will see what you write here, so say enough for it to make sense on its own.
absences.refuse_placeholder: Two people are already away that week

rates.title: What {person}'s time is worth
rates.hint: A rate is dated rather than changed, so a month already stated at the old one still means what it said. A raise is the old rate ending and a new one starting.
rates.none_yet: No rate on record. A statement for this person will show hours and no amount.

errors.date_required: Say which day this rate starts.
errors.bad_amount: Write the amount as a number, like 65 or 65.50.

rates.confirm_remove_body: Months already worked out keep the figures they were worked out with. Months from here on lose this rate.

statement.title: Before you invoice
statement.hint: What this month comes to at your rate, so the figure is agreed before the invoice is written rather than argued about after it arrives.
statement.no_rate: No rate on record for you yet, so this shows the hours only. Ask whoever looks after the team.
statement.still_moving: The month is still open, so these figures can still move.
statement.settled: The month is closed, so these figures are settled.

leave.title: {person}'s leave
leave.hint: Held in minutes, not days: a day is not a fixed quantity for anyone working uneven hours. The leave year runs from the anniversary of joining.
leave.none_yet: No leave year on record yet.

errors.dates_required: Say when the leave year starts and ends.
errors.backwards: The leave year cannot end before it starts.
errors.already_there: There is already an entry for this leave year.

leave.confirm_agree_body: {duration} can no longer be edited afterwards. A later change has to be recorded separately, with its own reason.

holidays.title: Public holidays
holidays.subtitle: The days nobody works. A holiday reduces the target for that day; it is not added to what was worked.
holidays.none_this_year: No days on this calendar for this year.
holidays.not_permitted_detail: Only a manager can change the calendar.

errors.date_and_name: Give the day a date and a name.

holidays.confirm_remove_body: {day} stops being a holiday, so everyone's target for that day goes back up.

shared.load_failed_detail: Something went wrong on the way. Try again, and tell whoever looks after the team if it keeps happening.

review_days.title: Days to look at for {person}
review_days.body: Hours that were counted on these days are no longer there. Say what happened to each one and the month can be closed.
review_days.all_settled: Nothing left to look at. This month can be closed.
review_days.placeholder: Entered on the wrong day and moved

refusals.absence_type_in_use: {in_use, plural, one {# absence is recorded as this kind, so it cannot be removed — the record of it would stop making sense.} other {# absences are recorded as this kind, so it cannot be removed — the record of them would stop making sense.}} Switch it off instead: it disappears from the list of kinds somebody can choose, and the existing ones stay readable.
refusals.month_settled: {month} has been {month_state}, so its records can no longer change. Ask for it to be reopened if this needs to go in.
refusals.last_manager: This is the only person who looks after the team. Taking it away would leave nobody able to reach anyone's month, and nobody able to give it back. Make somebody else a manager first.

detail.title: Hours in detail
detail.still_running: Still running — it has no length yet and counts nothing
detail.gone: This month counted it, and it is no longer there
detail.nothing_logged: Nothing was logged against a work item this month.
detail.other_subtitle: Meetings, admin, training, travel — and anything brought in from before. These are counted in the month too.
detail.footnote: Hours are counted wherever they were logged, in every workspace.
detail.rounding_note: Minutes are rounded once per day and project, so these subtotals need not add up to the figure above.
detail.running_note: {count, plural, one {# timer is still running. It has no length yet, so it counts nothing here.} other {# timers are still running. They have no length yet, so they count nothing here.}}
detail.missing_note: {count, plural, one {# entry this month counted can no longer be found. Only its identifier was kept, so there is nothing left to show.} other {# entries this month counted can no longer be found. Only their identifiers were kept, so there is nothing left to show.}}
detail.auto_stopped_hint: This timer was left running and closed at the maximum. The length is a ceiling, not a measurement — it needs correcting.
